title: Changing Your Habits for Better Health
source_name: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK)
text: The NIDDK provides evidence-based guidance for sustainable weight management through behavior change. Key principles involve creating a sustainable energy deficit by eating smaller portions, replacing high-calorie foods with lower-calorie nutrient-dense alternatives (like fruits and vegetables), and increasing physical activity. Fast, extreme weight loss is generally not recommended, as gradual changes in daily habits are more likely to lead to long-term success. Keeping a food and activity journal can improve awareness and support weight loss goals.
